message.hololith.no_room: The Hololith needs a clear 3 × 3 area.
gui.hololith.intensity.tooltip: Adjusts every Hololith projection on this client. Saved when this panel closes. No new survey is needed.
message.hololith.table_recorded: Table %s recorded. Use this card on reference markers.
message.hololith.table_card_hint: This card links markers to a table. Record a sensor or terrain to change a survey.
message.hololith.card_empty: Blank card: use a sensor or beacon, or sneak-use terrain to record coordinates.
message.hololith.table_linked_sensor: Survey linked to sensor %s. It follows the sensor while loaded.
message.hololith.table_linked_coordinate: Survey set to coordinates %s, %s. Loaded or cached terrain is required.
message.hololith.reference_linked: Reference linked to %s %s. Dye to recolor; sneak-wrench to unlink.
message.hololith.reference_card_hint: Record a sensor or sneak-use a table first. Coordinate cards cannot link markers.
message.hololith.sensor_recorded: Sensor %s recorded. Use this card on a table or reference markers.
message.hololith.coordinates_recorded: Coordinates %s, %s recorded. Use this card on a table.
message.hololith.reference_already_unlin: Reference is already unlinked. Use a recorded sensor or table card to link it.
message.hololith.reference_unlinked: Reference unlinked. It no longer appears on its previous survey.
message.hololith.reference_unlinked_hint: Reference unlinked. Apply a recorded sensor or table card to show it on a survey.
message.hololith.reference_status: Reference → %s %s · %s. Dye to recolor; sneak-wrench to unlink.
message.hololith.position_unavailable: Position unavailable. The card was not changed; try again when the platform is loaded.
tooltip.hololith.table.1: Place in a clear, dry 3 × 3 space; aim at the center.
tooltip.hololith.table.2: Empty hand: panel. Wrench: rotate; sneak-wrench: area.
tooltip.hololith.table.3: Link a sensor card to follow it. Park upright before disassembly.
tooltip.hololith.sensor: A movable survey location for linked tables.
tooltip.hololith.sensor.1: Use a Survey Card here, then on a table.
tooltip.hololith.sensor.2: Mount beneath a ship or on a Create contraption.
tooltip.hololith.sensor.3: Reports while ticking; the linked table scans loaded terrain.
tooltip.hololith.beacon: A remote survey location for your base or outpost.
tooltip.hololith.beacon.1: Use a Survey Card here, then on a distant table.
tooltip.hololith.beacon.2: Survey while the area is loaded to keep a cached map.
tooltip.hololith.beacon.3: Does not load chunks. Breaking it requires a new card link.
tooltip.hololith.marker: A colored reference pin on a linked terrain survey.
tooltip.hololith.marker.1: Apply a recorded sensor card or a sneak-recorded table card.
tooltip.hololith.marker.2: Dye: color. Sneak-wrench: unlink. Empty hand: inspect link.
tooltip.hololith.marker.3: Works enclosed; must be loaded and inside the surveyed area.
tooltip.hololith.card.1: Use on a sensor or beacon, then a table or reference marker.
tooltip.hololith.card.2: Sneak-use terrain for coordinates; sneak-use a table for marker links.
tooltip.hololith.card.3: Recording a new target replaces this card's previous target.
hololith.ponder.surveying_table.text_1: Place the table on a clear 3 x 3 floor. Its nine sections form one instrument.
hololith.ponder.surveying_table.text_2: The light projection preserves terrain height, water, trees and surface structures. This example surveys the tutorial model.
hololith.ponder.surveying_table.text_3: Right-click the table to open its controls: survey area, source, rotation, magnification and vertical relief.
hololith.ponder.surveying_table.text_4: Use a Create Wrench to turn the map by a quarter turn. The surveyed world stays in place.
hololith.ponder.surveying_table.text_5: Sneak-use the Wrench to cycle 32, 64 and 128 block survey areas. Larger areas cover more ground; 128 uses coarser samples.
hololith.ponder.surveying_table.text_6: Magnification enlarges the display. Vertical relief makes changes in elevation easier to read. Neither loads extra terrain.
hololith.ponder.survey_sources.text_1: A new table surveys around itself. A Survey Card can point it at a different source.
hololith.ponder.survey_sources.text_2: Use a Survey Card on a Local Survey Sensor to record its identity.
hololith.ponder.survey_sources.text_3: Use that card on the table. It follows the sensor's current world position, including supported moving ships and contraptions.
hololith.ponder.survey_sources.text_4: A Remote Survey Beacon links the same way. Leave one at a base to revisit that area's survey from another table.
hololith.ponder.survey_sources.text_5: Sneak-use a card on ordinary terrain to record coordinates, then apply it to the table. Exact coordinates can also be set in the controls.
hololith.ponder.survey_sources.text_6: Surveys use loaded terrain and refresh gradually. A saved projection stays visible when its source goes offline; distant chunks are never force-loaded.
hololith.ponder.reference_markers.text_1: Sneak-use a Survey Card on the table to copy its identity for Reference Markers.
hololith.ponder.reference_markers.text_2: Use the card on a placed marker. Its colored pin appears at the matching horizontal position in that table's known survey.
hololith.ponder.reference_markers.text_3: Use any of the sixteen dyes to recolor the physical marker and its pin. Choose your own colors for bases, routes and landmarks.
hololith.ponder.reference_markers.text_4: A sensor card can instead link markers to that sensor's survey group. Pins follow the map's rotation and scale; they are not entity trackers.
hololith.ponder.reference_markers.text_5: Sneak-use a Create Wrench on a marker to unlink it. The marker remains available to link again.
